q1_issues.issue: The restrictive "other" of "at other moon phases" is dropped, so the rule fires at any moon phase whatever — including the phase the contrast is there to exclude — which is a different and stronger claim than the sentence makes.
(Time $x moon_phase) puts a bare kind symbol in the Time slot, which is specified to carry structured calendar/clock terms or a deictic/named time constant, not a class.

q2_gaps: the alterity determiner "other" ("at other moon phases", "the other N"): nothing encodes the contrast set it presupposes, so the restriction can only be dropped or silently invented

a non-calendar recurring temporal frame ("at moon phases"): the Time terms are calendar/clock granularities (Year/Month/Day/Weekday/Hour/Minute) plus deictic constants and day-parts, with no slot for a domain-specific cycle
a capitalized plural group designation ("the Keepers"): whether it is a proper noun taking a name-derived symbol plus a Name atom, or an ordinary definite plural group witness, is not settled
notes: The change-of-kind consequent follows the prescribed shape exactly (Patient on the turn event, result state reified with the same subject as Experiencer, the flat copular atom, the Result link), and the three compound genus atoms plus the exposed adjectival chalky modifier are correct. Minting a per-occasion Skolem witness for the bare mass "salt-bloom" departs from the bare-class-symbol rule for non-specific objects, but it is what lets the definite anaphor "the salt-bloom" corefer in the consequent.
